note: Each playbook lists leading IIMs and global business schools that faced the same problem, the age and position they were at, what is documented that they did, and the documented result. 'ageThen' is the school's age at the time; the page compares it with the viewing IIM's age. Where a source states the result but not the method, the card says so.

pay.title: Pay far below the IIM A/B/C level

research.title: Research output per faculty below the leaders

faculty.title: Faculty capacity or depth under strain

women.title: Women's share below the peer group

credibility.title: Earn global credibility early
credibility.why: Pay and recruiter pull follow reputation. The leaders below sought their first international accreditation at about age 10-14, which is where the newer IIMs are now. None of the sources claims accreditation alone raised salaries; it is the documented first step leaders took, and it forces the faculty, research and learning standards that recruiters and rankings read.

analogs.situation: A decade-old school, founded 2001 with its first cohort that year.
did: Received AACSB accreditation on 2 December 2011, the first business school in South Asia to do so, timed with its 10th anniversary.
Later added AMBA (announced 2020), becoming one of the world's triple-accredited schools.
analogs.result: AACSB at age 10; triple accreditation by age 19.
analogs.caveat: The pages state dates and mission, not the steps ISB took to qualify.

analogs.situation: Founded in 1994 as a joint venture of the Shanghai government and the European Commission.
did: Won EQUIS in March 2004, the first school on the Chinese mainland to do so.
Added AACSB in December 2008, and has renewed both on cycle since.
analogs.result: In the Financial Times MBA top 25 every year from 2005 to 2026; 8th in 2026.

analogs.situation: Founded 1996, a second-generation IIM.
did: In 2010 became the first IIM accredited by AMBA.
In October 2021 became the fifth IIM to win EQUIS.
analogs.result: Double crown (AMBA and EQUIS); NIRF 2021 rank 4 is cited on the same page.
analogs.caveat: The institute credits 'all stakeholders' and does not describe the process.

analogs.situation: Founded 1996; first PGP batch in 1998.
did: AMBA on 13 October 2016, the fourth IIM to hold it.
AACSB in February 2019.
EQUIS on 10 December 2019, completing the Triple Crown.
Had set up a foreign tie-up (Lyon) in 2005, a Fellow Programme in 2006 and an International Advisory Board in 2021.
analogs.result: Triple Crown within 3 years of the first accreditation.

analogs.situation: Founded 2007.
did: AACSB, announced by AACSB International on 29 April 2026.
EQUIS, reported in the same newsletter.
analogs.result: Double accreditation at age 19, alongside a top-100 CEOWORLD listing.
analogs.caveat: The newsletter lists what EQUIS evaluates (faculty quality, research, internationalisation, corporate engagement) but not the changes Shillong made.

analogs.situation: Founded 2009; salary growth has slowed below the A/B/C pace.
did: Received the AMBA accreditation certificate at the AMBA & BGA Global Deans and Directors Conference 2026 in Madrid.
Debuted in the QS Executive MBA Rankings 2026.
analogs.result: First international accreditation at age 17.

src.t: IIM Ranchi newsletter, Raconteur V13 N2

analogs.situation: Founded 2015, closest in age to IIM Sirmaur.
did: Took AACSB membership and began the accreditation process.

Hosted its AACSB mentor for a campus visit and worked on the Initial Self-Evaluation Report roadmap, covering strategic goals, faculty qualifications, learner success, research influence and assurance of learning.
analogs.result: In progress; no accreditation date given.

src.t: MediaInfoline: IIM Sambalpur advances towards AACSB

credibility.notDocumented: No source shows how much accreditation moved salaries or recruiter counts, and none of the schools published the internal steps it took to qualify. No international accreditation was found for IIM Jammu or IIM Sirmaur.

research.title: Build a research base while the faculty is being built
research.why: Research per faculty is the metric where the newer IIMs trail most (Shillong 0.61, Sirmaur 0.74 against 0.96). The leaders below built research capacity in their first two decades, in different ways: a fully Ph.D. faculty measured on top-journal output, partner-school mentoring, and early foreign training.

analogs.situation: Founded 1991. In 2000, at age 9, it first entered the Financial Times list and was ranked 40th in research, measured by faculty publications in top journals.
did: Grew faculty from 11 to 136 in nine years while staying among the only 15 ranked schools with a 100% Ph.D.-qualified faculty.
Measured itself on top-journal publications from its first ranking entry.

src.t: HKUST: Business School enters the Financial Times world list (2000)
HKUST: top 10 in the world for MBA and business research (2010)

analogs.caveat: The school's releases state the ranks and faculty growth, not the incentives or hiring rules behind them.

analogs.situation: A new school needing research credibility without a long-built faculty.
did: Combined resident faculty with visiting faculty from its founding partners (Wharton, Kellogg, London Business School).
Senior partner-school faculty serve as Area Leaders and help with curriculum, faculty recruitment and research mentorship.
Offers individual and area research budgets, research associates and grants from its research centres.
analogs.result: A research-driven faculty model in place from the first cohort.

analogs.situation: A new IIM with no experienced faculty, set up with Ford Foundation funding and Harvard Business School as partner.
did: Sent its first batches of recruited faculty to HBS for the nine-month International Teachers Programme, which taught them to teach and write cases and brought the case method to India.

Ravi Matthai (director from 1965) judged that the HBS arrangement should be upgraded or ended; it ended. The article notes it had no research collaboration, IIMA faculty could not teach at HBS, and IIMA was becoming known as a branch of HBS. He fostered faculty freedom, including to pursue their own research.
analogs.result: A home-grown faculty and research culture; the IIMA-HBS arrangement was discontinued.

src.t: T T Ram Mohan: Ravi Matthai and IIMA, a story of institution-building (IIM Indore Management Journal, 2011)

analogs.caveat: The article's lesson is that a foreign partner trained the faculty but did not share research, so independence had to be built.

analogs.situation: Founded 2015; faculty grew from 12 to 74 between 2021 and 2026 in NIRF filings.
did: Method not published.
analogs.result: Journal articles in OpenAlex rose from 17 (2021) to 88 (2025).
analogs.caveat: Output rose in step with faculty growth; the policy behind it is not documented.

analogs.school: SMU Lee Kong Chian School of Business (Singapore)
analogs.situation: Founded in 2000, still a small faculty; its own dean said results came despite a relatively small faculty.
did: Hires faculty on the basis of research or recognised expertise in their field.
Reported a record 11 new faculty hired in a single summer in a later year.
analogs.result: UT Dallas research ranking 49th (2016) to 40th (2017); FT Asia-Pacific MBA 13th (2017) to 6th (2018); in 2024 1st in Singapore and 2nd in Asia in the FT research-impact ranking.

src.t: SMU: LKCSB moves up 7 notches, 6th in FT Asia-Pacific 2018
SMU: business school 3rd in Asia in research rankings
SMU: LKCSB ranked 1st in Singapore for research impact (2024)

analogs.caveat: The sources give ranks and the hiring basis, not specific incentives.

analogs.school: Haskayne School of Business, University of Calgary (Canada)
analogs.situation: An established school ranked 11th for articles in its priority journals in 2015.
did: Built the Eyes High Journal List of 63 high-impact journals, 35 of them designated Star journals, to tell faculty where to aim.
Its associate dean of research credits faculty for rising to the challenge of targeting these publications.
analogs.result: 5th for Eyes High Star articles in 2019, and 4th when weighted by Ph.D. faculty size.

src.t: University of Calgary: Haskayne dramatically improves research rankings

analogs.caveat: The article does not mention incentives, hiring or workload changes.

analogs.situation: An established school whose research rank in 2006 was 32 places below its 2019 rank.
did: Rapidly increased financial and technical support for faculty research projects, in the dean's words.
Instituted and refined annual Research Reports to track and strengthen faculty performance.
Hired faculty who do superb research.
analogs.result: Research rank 20th worldwide in 2019 and 13th in 2018.

src.t: Boston College Carroll School: Financial Times

analogs.caveat: The dean's account; the school does not publish the budget or the incentive terms.

research.notDocumented: Per-paper incentives, teaching-load relief and seed grants are not stated in the sources found. Haskayne and Boston College are established schools, so they show methods rather than what to do at age 11-19.

faculty.title: Scale the faculty without diluting quality
faculty.why: Newer IIMs are adding faculty quickly, and it shows in the data: Shillong grew from 32 to 81 listed faculty but its Ph.D. share fell from 100% to 87.7%; Sambalpur grew from 12 to 74 and held about 95%; Sirmaur's listed faculty has not grown while its class has.

analogs.situation: Student body up from 235 to 2,680 in nine years.
did: Expanded faculty from 11 to 136 in the same period.
Remained one of only 15 ranked schools with a 100% Ph.D.-qualified faculty.
analogs.result: Faculty grew twelve-fold without a reported fall in doctoral share.

src.t: HKUST: Business School enters the Financial Times world list

analogs.situation: Needed breadth of courses before a large resident faculty existed.
did: A portfolio of resident and visiting faculty from top US, European, Singapore and Indian schools.
Partner-school Area Leaders took part in faculty recruitment.
analogs.result: Course breadth from the first batches while resident faculty grew.

analogs.situation: Faculty listed in NIRF grew from 32 to 81.
did: Hired fast across areas.
analogs.result: Ph.D. share fell from 100% to 87.7% over the same period, the trade-off of rapid hiring.

analogs.situation: Faculty listed in NIRF grew from 12 to 74.
did: Hired six-fold in five years.
analogs.result: Kept a Ph.D. share of about 95% (92.9% to 95.4% across editions).

faculty.notDocumented: None of these sources publishes its hiring criteria or how it protected doctoral quality during rapid hiring.

international.title: Build international exposure into the model
international.why: International students are 0% at IIM Sirmaur and about 0-1% at every IIM in the dataset. The global schools below built international faculty and partners in from the start, not later.

analogs.situation: Nine years old and in its first Financial Times ranking.
did: Built an internationally recruited faculty.
analogs.result: Ranked 4th in the world for international faculty and 3rd for international course content.

src.t: HKUST: Business School enters the Financial Times world list

analogs.caveat: The release states the result; recruitment tactics are not described.

analogs.situation: A new school in Shanghai.
did: Founded as a joint venture of the Shanghai government and the European Commission, with Shanghai Jiao Tong University and EFMD as executive partners.
analogs.result: EQUIS in 2004, and campuses in Beijing, Shenzhen, Accra and Zurich.

analogs.situation: A new school with no international reputation.
did: Opened with founding partners Wharton, Kellogg and London Business School supplying visiting faculty and Area Leaders.
analogs.result: International faculty exposure from the first cohort.

analogs.situation: Founded 2009.
did: Runs a Student Exchange Programme (STEP) since 2014.
analogs.result: Reports about 100 exchange students from over 60 business schools and about 200 international students from 30+ countries (page undated).

analogs.situation: Founded 2015.
did: Signed its first foreign exchange MoU with ALBA (Greece) for a trimester exchange at no extra academic fee; more are under negotiation.
analogs.result: Exchange route opened; inbound totals not published.

analogs.situation: A mature leader with almost no international students in its two-year programme.
did: Built an exchange network: in 2013, more than 60 foreign business schools offered more than 120 seats to about 424 students, with seats expected to rise to about 150.
Hosted nearly 75 exchange students from foreign schools on campus and ran an International Student Exchange Fair through its student Exchange Council with the Student Exchange Office.
Its PGP-FABM programme takes incoming exchange students from ESSEC, UBC, Shanghai Jiao Tong and NHH for a term at IIMA.
analogs.result: International exposure through exchange, not through enrolment: the share of international degree students is still about 0.3%.

src.t: IIM Ahmedabad: international student exchange fair 2013 (press release)

analogs.caveat: The figures are from 2013; a current inbound count was not found.

analogs.situation: A leading global school, founded in 1957.
did: Operates campuses in France, Singapore and Abu Dhabi; one alumnus says the Singapore expansion was pivotal to where the school is today.
No single nationality holds a majority of the class.
analogs.result: Class of 2016 was 93% international, against about 35% at Harvard Business School and 40% at Stanford.
analogs.caveat: A result and a campus footprint; INSEAD's admissions method is not documented in the sources found. A further claim of a 10% nationality cap rests on one source and is not used.

international.notDocumented: No source gives the share of international students at any of these schools at the matching age. The IIMA exchange figures are from 2013 and INSEAD's admissions method is not documented in the sources found.

gender.title: Raise women's share
gender.why: Women are 25-34% of students at IIM Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Calcutta and Sirmaur, against 48-68% at Shillong, Jammu and Sambalpur. The newer IIMs show what policy can do; Harvard shows what a mature leader did.

analogs.situation: Before 2017 women were under 11% of MBA classes across the IIMs, Sambalpur included.
did: Gave female candidates an additional 5% cut-off reduction when calling for interviews, then ranked everyone on a common merit list.
analogs.result: Its director reports 50% female enrolment from 2017 onwards; the 2024-26 batch was 76% women, though the 2025-27 batch was 33%.

analogs.situation: Founded 1996.
did: Added 60 supernumerary seats for women, the first IIM to do so.
analogs.result: Intake of women guaranteed whatever the selection criteria.

src.t: Careers360: How IIM Kozhikode changed the game

analogs.situation: A century-old school where women were 25% of the class of 1985 and 35% about ten years before 2014.
did: Under Dean Nitin Nohria (from 2010), made gender a priority and launched a Gender Initiative.
Pledged to more than double the share of women protagonists in its cases to 20% within five years.
Launched a recruitment programme targeting women.
analogs.result: A record 41% of the entering MBA class were women in 2014.

src.t: The Harvard Crimson: Tackling gender inequality at HBS
Fortune: Harvard B-school dean offers unusual apology (2014)
GMAT Club: HBS launches recruitment programme targeting women

analogs.caveat: Not stage-matched (a mature school). Figures are from news reports of the dean's statements.

analogs.situation: Women were 28.6% of PG students in 2026.
did: Its 2026 admissions policy reserves 40 seats for female applicants through a separate admission route.
analogs.result: The effect will show from the 2026-28 batch.

gender.notDocumented: How the 76% at Sambalpur was sustained or why the next batch fell to 33% is not explained in the sources found.

sustain.title: Keep growth going past the first decade
sustain.why: Ranchi (4.8% a year) and Shillong (3.9% over the last three years) are growing slower than the 5.8% A/B/C pace at ages 17-19, and Ahmedabad and Bangalore have slowed at maturity. The schools below kept climbing through the same ages.

analogs.situation: Twenty years old and already top-ranked in India.
did: Method not published in the sources found.
analogs.result: Median salary up 12% in 2021, a pandemic year, and about 15% in 2022; offers reported rising from 1,195 to 2,072.
analogs.caveat: Reports differ on the size of the gains and use mid-80% or whole-batch figures.

analogs.situation: Eighteen to twenty years old and already inside the top 20.
did: Moved up the Financial Times MBA ranking while its research rank rose from 17th to 10th and its doctoral placement rank rose 20 places.
analogs.result: MBA 17th (2008), 16th (2009), 6th (2011), record high.
analogs.caveat: The school's releases pair the MBA rise with the research rise but do not state a cause.

analogs.situation: First entered the Financial Times MBA top 25 at about age 11.
did: Held EQUIS (2004) and AACSB (2008) and renewed them on cycle.
analogs.result: Stayed in the FT MBA top 25 for more than 20 consecutive years, including ten as Asia's No. 1.

analogs.situation: A mature leader whose median pay growth has slowed to about 3% a year (2022-25).
did: Became the first IIM to set up an international campus, in Dubai, with its first programme from September 2025.
analogs.result: Too early to measure.

src.t: Careers360: IIM Ahmedabad to set up Dubai campus

analogs.caveat: The article names neither the programme nor the reason.

analogs.situation: A mature leader whose recent pay growth has slowed to about 1% a year (2022-25).
did: Announced two undergraduate programmes in July 2025, a BSc (Honours) in Economics and a data-science BSc, each four years with an intake of 40.
analogs.result: Too early to measure; one report cites about 12,000 applications by December 2025.

src.t: IIM Bangalore Digest: UG programmes in Economics and Data Science

analogs.caveat: IIMB's announcement page could not be opened directly; details come from the report and search summaries of it.

sustain.notDocumented: No fix for a shrinking recruiter base was found; IIM Ranchi's count was 124 (2023), 76 (2024) and 81 (2025) in one aggregator, and sources conflict. The IIM Ahmedabad and Bangalore moves are too recent to show results, and no source explains why ISB, HKUST or CEIBS kept growing at ages 15-20.

recruiters.title: Rebuild and widen the recruiter base
recruiters.why: IIM Ranchi's recruiter count fell from 124 (2023) to 77 (2026), against 187 on average at IIM A/B/C. The cases below show what a recruiter base looks like when it grows at ages 11-19, and the one school that documents how it rebuilt its own.

analogs.situation: An established school that decided its recruiting was too transactional.
did: Merged the career centre and corporate relations so they 'work hand-in-glove'.
Put staff in the field, with team members in the eastern and western US, Europe, the Middle East and Shanghai.
Brought in Boston Consulting Group, which conceived many of the strategies in corporate relations and career services.
Moved recruiting from a transactional model to a relationship-based one.
analogs.result: In one year, 14 companies planned to hire more Olin graduates and 15 hired Olin graduates for the first time; internship recruiting, new on-campus firms and alumni engagement also grew.

src.t: Olin Business School: Retooled career center and corporate relations yields big results

analogs.caveat: A school publication, so the results are self-reported. The overall placement numbers are not given.

analogs.situation: Founded 2007; 73 recruiters in 2022.
did: Method not published.
analogs.result: Recruiters doubled to 147 by 2026 as median pay rose from ₹22.3 L to ₹25 L (2022-2025).
analogs.caveat: Counts are from aggregator sites; none explains how the base was widened.

analogs.situation: Founded 2015; 125 participating firms in 2023, 65+ of them new recruiters.
did: Method not published.
analogs.result: About 250 participating firms by 2025.
analogs.caveat: The 2025 count is from news and placement sites and may include summer recruiters.

analogs.situation: Founded 2015, a non-metro campus.
did: Method not published.
analogs.result: More than 180 recruiters took part in the 2024-26 batch, over 100 of them first-time recruiters.
analogs.caveat: Another tally gives 201 recruiters, 141 of them new, so the counts conflict.

analogs.situation: Founded 2016.
did: Method not published.
analogs.result: Recruiters up from 200 to 260 in a year.
analogs.caveat: Counts are from an aggregator site.

recruiters.notDocumented: No Indian institute documents how it widened its recruiter base; the IIM cases are outcomes only. IIM Ranchi's count was 124 (2023), 76 (2024) and 81 (2025) in one aggregator, and sources conflict. Olin documents a method but is an established US school, not a peer.
